correctness.rationale: The source circuit gives six disjoint Bell pairs exactly. Independent local bit flips make each pair a Bell-diagonal mixture with error probability \(q=2p(1-p)\), and standard Bell teleportation turns that mixture into a bit-flip channel. The source Eq. (36) family has exact overlap structure yielding \(F_{\mathrm{Bi}}=1-2q(1-q)(2a^2-1)^2\); \(p=1/2,a=0\) gives \(1/2\). The bundled checker corroborates the algebra with exact rational arithmetic; the proof itself is symbolic.

evidence: Bowen and Bose prove that standard teleportation with an arbitrary two-qubit mixed resource acts as a generalized Pauli/depolarizing channel with weights equal to Bell-state components.
For the independently bit-flipped Bell pair here, those Bell weights are exactly \(1-q\) on \(\Phi^+\) and \(q\) on \(\Psi^+\).

value.rationale: The false statement is highlighted in the abstract and results discussion as a robustness advantage. Under the stated independent local bit-flip model the error is large on the paper's own plotted family: \(F_{\mathrm{Bi}}=1/2\) at \(p=1/2,a=0\). The correction distinguishes ordinary local decoherence from a specially correlated global flip, which materially changes the physical interpretation of the claimed immunity.
